For parents

Parents don't come for the technique. They come for what shows up at home and at school.

We use jiu-jitsu to work on focus, independence, getting along with teammates and facing a challenge without giving up. The tools are respect, discipline, perseverance and humility, the same ones we ask of every adult on the mat.

Teens get a class of their own.

Juniors starts at 6:50 pm, Monday to Thursday, the same start time as our adult evening class.

Your child doesn't have to compete.

Competing is for the kids and teens who want it. Everyone else has a full place on the team.

You're not left waiting in the car.

A seating area with sofas for parents, a reception desk, restrooms and ample parking.

    Frequently asked questions

    01I've never trained. Can I really start?

    Yes. Tell us your age, experience and goal when you book. We recommend the right class and confirm the time, and beginners start with the fundamentals.

    02Is it safe for my child?

    Jiu-jitsu is a grappling art, with no striking. Classes are grouped by age, and Professor Fred is on the mat. It's still a contact activity, and we won't promise anyone an injury-free path.

    03Will my child become aggressive?

    Self-defense is part of what we teach. So are respect, humility and care for your training partner.

    04Will the professor really pay attention to my child, or to me?

    Fred teaches the classes and is on the mat every day. The close relationship between professor, students and families is central to how Lobo works.

    05My child is nervous about trying. What do I do?

    Tell us when you book. The trial class lets your child meet Fred and see the room, and parents have a seating area with sofas.

    06Does my child, or do I, have to compete?

    No. Competing is an invitation, never an expectation. If you want to, we prepare and guide you.
